items_missed: No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation — jumped straight from 'what date' into data collection
Never asked how many boxes — started the question ('And box wise, are they getting like?'), said 'Go ahead,' and never came back to it
Never asked about packing services or quoted packing pricing
No special-considerations probe (long walk from a 3rd-floor unit to the truck, narrow stairwells, tight turns) despite third floor with no elevator
No parking/loading-access question at either the apartment or the storage facility
Never asked the moving-stressors question — customer volunteered 'this is my first time making a move' and the rep did not acknowledge it at all
No Worries Damage Coverage never explained — said 'insurance' is included but never the $2,000 repair/replace/reimburse pitch or the 60¢/lb baseline
No full 'no hidden fees' pitch (no credit card fees, no fuel surcharge, no assembly fees) — only a generic 'everything's included'
No 'does that make sense?' sense-check after the clock/pricing monologue
Walk distance never raised as an estimate variable
No equivalents/anchoring reference used to make the time range concrete
Bed and dresser disassembly confirmed as included but never factored into the time estimate
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech missing — no prep-shortens-the-move framing, no consolidation examples, no 'take a carload' tip
No booking attempt — customer said she had availability confirmed for the 24th and the rep offered an email instead of asking to lock it in, then let her leave to call two competitors
Never mentioned the BOLDED detail list at the top of the confirmation email or asked her to reply with corrections
Never gave office hours or how to reach the team
Never used the customer's name once after collecting it
top_strength: The pricing and clock explanation was clear and genuinely useful — he gave a real two-scenario dollar range ($891 at four hours, $1,095 at five), showed his math including the $75 transportation fee, and proactively answered the customer's traffic worry by explaining that drive time to her door is outside the hourly rate and that arrival after 9:00 triggers a late-arrival discount.
coaching_note: Angela told you 'this is my first time making a move' and then walked off the call to price two competitors — that was the whole opportunity and it went by untouched. A first-time mover is exactly who the Save Your Ass prep speech, No Worries coverage, and Meet Your Mover are built for, and none of the three got said. Next call: when a customer flags they're new to this, stop and say 'let me tell you what I'd tell a friend moving for the first time,' run the prep speech, then close on it — 'we've got the 24th open, there's no deposit and no cancellation fee, want me to hold it for you?' You already had the availability and the no-deposit angle in hand; you just never asked for the booking.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and patient with a few light affirmations ('Yeah, for sure', 'I gotcha') and the customer ended positive, but the rep never used her name, delivered pricing as one long unbroken monologue, and let her 'first time moving' comment pass without a word of empathy.
audio_review_reason: Heavy transcription garbling in the rep's speech (opening greeting rendered as 'Hi mo. How Isis Chris?', multiple run-on unpunctuated stretches) makes it impossible to tell from text alone whether the delivery was genuinely rushed and mumbled or whether this is ASR noise — worth a listen before coaching on pace and clarity.
